outcomes.text: Identify the expressed or understood subject of a non-finite clause.
Choose the form of the infinitival in active, passive and interrogative constructions.
Apply auxiliary order and recognise a participial modifier without adding a relative marker.

key_terms.definition: A clause whose verb is an infinitival or participial form, as in to check the gauge or checking the gauge.
An infinitival with a plain-form verb and without the marker to.
A subject present as words in the clause, as him is in for him to speak.

options.feedback: Him is the expressed subject of the infinitival after for.
Him is the expressed subject of the infinitival after for.
Him is the expressed subject of the infinitival after for.

opening.prompt: Who is understood to speak in “They arranged for him to speak first”?

options.feedback: Passive causative make selects a to-infinitival.
Passive causative make selects a to-infinitival.
Passive causative make selects a to-infinitival.

opening.prompt: Which is the ordinary passive counterpart of “They made us wait”?

options.feedback: Checking heads a participial modifier. That is checking would be a finite relative.
Checking heads a participial modifier. That is checking would be a finite relative.
Checking heads a participial modifier. That is checking would be a finite relative.

opening.prompt: Choose a non-finite modifier for “the technician ___ the meter”.

options.text: It’s essential for she to check the reading.
options.feedback: The order is for, accusative subject her, then the to-infinitival predicate.

options.text: It’s essential for her to check the reading.
options.feedback: The order is for, accusative subject her, then the to-infinitival predicate.

options.text: It’s essential for the reading her to check.
options.feedback: The order is for, accusative subject her, then the to-infinitival predicate.

opening.prompt: Which order fits the infinitival after essential?

options.feedback: The caller is understood. Who asks which person should receive the call.
The caller is understood. Who asks which person should receive the call.
The caller is understood. Who asks which person should receive the call.

opening.prompt: What role does who have in “They asked who to call”?

options.text: Nina believed herself to be ready.
options.feedback: Believe takes the overt object herself in this frame, and she is used in the finite alternative she was ready.

options.text: Nina believed she to be ready.
options.feedback: Believe takes the overt object herself in this frame, and she is used in the finite alternative she was ready.
Believe takes the overt object herself in this frame, and she is used in the finite alternative she was ready.

closing.prompt: Choose the ordinary active infinitival construction with believe to describe Nina’s view of herself.

options.feedback: The active causative takes a bare infinitival. The to form appears in the passive counterpart.
The active causative takes a bare infinitival. The to form appears in the passive counterpart.
The active causative takes a bare infinitival. The to form appears in the passive counterpart.

closing.prompt: In “The supervisor made Jen check again”, which words form the lower predicate?

options.feedback: In the infinitival, plain have selects been, and progressive been selects checking.
In the infinitival, plain have selects been, and progressive been selects checking.
In the infinitival, plain have selects been, and progressive been selects checking.

closing.prompt: Which order puts perfect have before progressive be?

options.text: They asked what Mara should check.
options.feedback: The finite question can express Mara as subject. The third option is grammatical but leaves the subject understood.

options.text: They asked what for Mara to check.
options.feedback: The finite question can express Mara as subject. The third option is grammatical but leaves the subject understood.
The finite question can express Mara as subject. The third option is grammatical but leaves the subject understood.

closing.prompt: Choose the finite wording if Mara must be named as the person who checks something.

options.text: the worker holding the spare meter
options.feedback: Holding the spare meter is participial and can modify worker without a relative marker.

options.text: the worker who holding the spare meter
options.feedback: Holding the spare meter is participial and can modify worker without a relative marker.

options.text: the worker who is holding the spare meter
options.feedback: Holding the spare meter is participial and can modify worker without a relative marker.

closing.prompt: Which version directly modifies the noun with a non-finite clause?
